sentences.text: 1  JUDGMENT

The petitioner has filed the present claim petition against the respondents under section 166 of MV Act seeking compensation towards the accidental injuries from date of accident till the date of payment together with cost and interest.

2. The factual matrix of the petition in the nutshell is as follows:
On 14.10.2023 at about 6.30 p.m., the petitioner was traveling in a NWKSRTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-31- F-1515 at NH-69, Sulemurki Cross, Gerusoppa Honnavara,
Uttar Karnataka District.
The said bus was proceeding from Sagara to Honnavara.
At that time the driver of NWKSRTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-31-F-1515 drove his vehicle in rash and negligent manner and dumped into a pit.
Due to the impact of accident, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries to various parts of the body.

3. Immediately after the accident, the petitioner was shifted to Government Hospital wherein first aid treatment was given and then he was taken to Kasturba Hospital wherein he was admitted as in inpatient.

X-ray report reveals that petitioner sustained D-12 Burst fracture causing spinal canal narrowing thereby impinging on the terminal cord and he was discharged with an advice for continuing follow up treatment with complete bed rest.

4. The petitioner further pleaded that he has incurred Rs.3,50,000/- towards hospitalization,
conveyance, medical treatment, attendant, nursing care and other incidental expenses.
He is in need of future medical treatment and other incidental expenses.
5. Petitioner further submits that, he was hale and healthy and was aged about 45 years as on the date of accident.
He was working as Labourer and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
He was maintaining his family out of said source of income and was a sole bread earner to his family.
Due to the accidental injuries he could not able to do any kind of work compared to his previous strategy.
The disability sustained in the accident has impacted on his earning capacity and as such himself and his family have suffered a lot by mentally, physically and financially.
6. The accident has taken place due to the rash and negligent driver of the respondent No.2, who drive his vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-31-F-1515.

The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the said vehicle thereby the vicarious liability is operated on respondent No.1 on the indemnified contract and as such, the respondents are liable to pay the compensation.
7. The respondent No.1 is the insurer and respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle,
are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, prays to award compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest from the date of accident till realization.
8. After registration of the petition, notices were issued against respondents.
Inspite of service of the notice, the respondent No.2 has not appeared before this court.
Hence, after due service of notice against the respondent No.2, the respondent No.2 is placed exparte.

In pursuance of service of Shankar G vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79862250/
2 notice the respondent No.1 has appeared through its counsels and filed their written statement on behalf of respondent No.1 by denying the entire petition averments.

prays to dismiss the petition.
9. In order to substantiate his claim, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and got marked 20 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20.
In addition to his evidence, the petitioner got examined the medical record Department as PW.2.
Further, the petitioner got examined the doctor, who has issued disability certificate for the injuries sustained by the petitioner as PW.3.
Thereby the evidence of petitioner side was completed and case was posted for respondent evidence.
On 21.03.2025 leaned counsel for the respondent No.1 has submitted that there is no respondent evidence on behalf of respondents.
Hence, prayed to post the case for the arguments.
Prayer was taken on record.

As per the prayer of learned counsel for respondent No.2, the respondent evidence was taken as closed and the case was posted for arguments.

2.

If so, what amount and from whom?
3 . What Order or Award?

17. The accident in question is not in dispute.

Whereas Ex.P.1 is the FIR with statement, Ex.P.3 is the spot sketch, Ex.P.4 is the spot mahazar, Ex.P.5 is the IMV report, Ex.P6 is the charge sheet which clearly shows that, on the alleged date, time and place of the accident has occurred and in the said accident the offender vehicle is involved in the occurrence of the same.
18. The above referred documents clearly indicates that, the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the respondent No.2 offender vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA-31-F-1515.

sentences.text: Pecuniary loss:-

This head of compensation includes compensation towards the loss of earning capacity, medical and future medical expenditure, expenditure incurred towards conveyance allowance, attendant charges, special diet and other miscellaneous expenditure.
As such these aspects are to be examined by examining the available materials on record.

(A) Loss of earning capacity and loss of future income/earnings:-
In order to determine the compensation under this head, it is necessary to consider the age of injured person, occupation, quantum of income, nature of injuries,
percentage of disability and multiplier applicable are to be worked out on the available materials.
(i) The age and applicable multiplier:- The petitioner has contended in his petition that, as on the date of accident he was aged about 45 years.

The material pertaining to Cr.No.202/23 and other medical documents contemplated as on the date of accident,
the petitioner was aged about 45 years.
In this regard, the petitioner has not produced any documents.
As per the medical records the age of the petitioner was 51 years as on the date accident.
So, as on the date of the accident the petitioner was aged 51 years.
As per the documentary evidence available on record, the age of the petitioner is considered as 51 years as on the date of the accident.

Applying the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and Others Case reported in 2009 ACJ SC 1298,
the multiplier of 11 is applicable to the present content.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and Others Case reported in 2009 ACJ SC 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, the multiplier of 11 is considered to determine the claim made herein.
(ii) The occupation of petitioner and quantum of income:- The petitioner has contended that, prior to the accident he was hale and healthy and was Labourer., and he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
He has not produced any documents to prove the said income.
Hence, in the absence of express proof, it is necessary to determine the income of the petitioner based on the principles of notional income.
The Karnataka State Legal Service Authority has fixed a chart for notional income.
By placing reliance on the said income slab.
The income of the petitioner is to be determined.
As per the said chart the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/- per month as operated to the year 2023.
The annual income of the petitioner shall arrive at Rs.1,92,000/- (Rs.16,000 X 12)

(iii) Nature of injury and percentage of disability:- To prove the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner he has examined one doctor Nagaraj.B.N., Orthopedic Surgeon at SOADS, Bengaluru, is examined as PW.2 and got marked 2 documents as per Ex.P.19 and Ex.P.20.
PW.2/doctor has deposed that, the petitioner has sustained D12 burst fracture with neurological deficits.

This witness has opined that, petitioner falls in the 4th category i.e., radiologically demonstrable instability with fracture or fracture dislocation with persistent pain, hence he has a disability of 30%.
The injuries are permanent in nature.

Petitioner has contended that, he is a labourer and assessed disability Shankar G vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79862250/
5 causes effect on the avocation of petitioner.

sentences.text: Hence, the disability is considered at 30%.
The said extent of disability is considerable to determine the compensation under this head.

To prove the nature of his injuries the petitioner has examined one Vignesh.N., Medical Record Department, Kasturba Hospital, Udupi is examined as PW.2, though him, authorization letter,
accident register, police intimation, out patient file, CT scan film and x-rays are marked under Ex.P.13 to Ex.18.

These documents shows that petitioner has taken treatment in Kasturba Hospital,
Manipal.
Annual income X Multiplier X permanent physical disability = Loss of earning capacity.
Rs.1,92,000 X 11 X 30/100= Rs.6,33,600/-. Thereby the petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.6,33,600/- towards loss of earning capacity and future earnings.
The petitioner being a Labourer and contended that, he used to earn Rs.20,000/- per month.
As the petitioner has not produced any documents to prove his income.
In the absence of proof, the notional income is considered as Rs.16,000/- per month.
Under the circumstances, the per day income of the petitioner would arrive at Rs.534/-.
As per the discharge summary the petitioner was admitted to hospital as an inpatient for 6 days and after discharge from the hospital there must be necessary to take bed rest for at least 24 days.
So, the petitioner is entitled to compensation towards laid up period with one attendant charge at the same rate which comes to Rs.32,040/- (30 days X 534 = Rs.16,020 + 16,020).
(B) Medical expenditure:-
The petitioner contended that, he has incurred Rs.3,50,000/- towards hospitalization, conveyance, medical treatment, attendant and nursing care expenses.
The petitioner has placed his reliance on medical bills.
On perusal of the same it is arrived at Rs.56,836/- as per Ex.P.8.
Further the petitioner also produced the ambulance bill for a sum of Rs.30,900/- as per Ex.P.10.
Hence, he is entitled for the same.
(C) Future medical expenditure
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards future medical expenditure for follow up treatment.
The medical record shows that the petitioner required further medical expenses.
In Nagaappa V/s Gurudayal Singh (2003) 2 SCC 274 the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "M.V.Act does not provide for passing of further award after final award is passed.

Therefore, in a case where injury to a victim requires periodical medical expenses, fresh award cannot be passed or previous award cannot be reviewed when the medical expenses are incurred after finalisation of the compensation proceedings.

Hence, only alternative is that at the time of passing of final award,
Tribunal/Court should consider such eventuality and fix compensation accordingly.

No one can Shankar G vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79862250/
6 suggest that it is improper to take into account expenditure genuinely and reasonably required to be incurred for future medical expenses.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Future medical expenses required to be incurred can be determined only on the basis of fair guess-work after taking into account increase in the cost of medical treatment.
It would be difficult to hold that for future medical expenses which are required to be incurred by a victim, fresh award could be passed."

Further, in Laxman @ Laxman Mourya V/s Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.,
and another reported in (2011) 10 SCC 756 the Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically stated that "there is no restriction that the Tribunal/Court cannot award compensation amount exceeding the claim amount."

entities.text:
Laxman @ Laxman Mourya V/s Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.,
and another reported in (2011) 10 SCC 756
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, this tribunal arrives at conclusion that the petitioner required future medical expenses of Rs.40,000/- under this head.
(D) Conveyance allowances, attendant charge and special diet:-
As per the available material it is clear that the petitioner was under treatment for a period of 6 days with extended follow up treatment.
This shows that petitioner has incurred expenditure towards conveyance to meet her treatment.

In Master Ayush v. Branch Manager, Reliance General Insurance Company Limited and Another, (2022) 7 SCC 738 the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that:
"The compensation under the head of conveyance ought to be granted on the higher side as the appellant was completely disabled and must have received help from family members or friends to get admitted at the hospital and back.

entities.text: Master Ayush v. Branch Manager, Reliance General Insurance Company Limited and Another, (2022) 7 SCC 738
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, it would be reasonable to award conveyance charges of Rs.50,000/-."
Applying the same formula to the case on hand, it is necessary to award compensation of Rs.50,000/- towards conveyance.

Further the petitioner has sustained fracture injuries in the accident and has taken assistance of attendant including the assistance of his family members, for which they have suffered loss of income.
This shows that the petitioner has sustained loss towards attendants.
Further the petitioner has sustained fracture injury and attended medication.
This shows that the petitioner has followed the nutrition to meet with her necessary protein and special diet.
By considering all these aspects, it is necessary to award compensation of Rs.30,000/- towards attendant charges and special diet.
In total, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.80,000/- under this head.
20. Non-Pecuniary Loss:-

entities.text: Shankar G vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon

sentences.text: According to medical records, the petitioner has sustained fracture injuries at the age of 51 years as on the date of accident.
The said accidental injuries have caused him lot of pain to suffer in his future life span.
In The Civil Appeal No. 8510 Of 2022 Sidram V/S The Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
And Anr, Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that "Pain and suffering would be categorized as a non-pecuniary loss as it is incapable of being arithmetically calculated.

Therefore, when compensation is to be awarded for pain and suffering, special circumstances of the claimant have to be taken into account including the victim's age, the unusual deprivation the victim has suffered, the effect thereof on his or her future life."

Like wise, in the case of Subulaxmi V/s Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation and another (2012) 10 SCC 177 the Hon'ble Supreme Court awarded compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- towards pain and sufferings to the petitioner.

entities.text: Subulaxmi V/s Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation and another (2012) 10 SCC 177
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applying the above formula to the case on hand and by considering the nature of the injuries and percentage of disability caused to the petitioner, the petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- under this head.

(b) Loss of enjoyment of life and amenities of life:-
The available on records reveals that the petitioner has sustained fracture injuries at the age of 51 years as on the date of accident.
In R.D. Hattangadi V/s M/s Pest Control (India) Private Ltd., (1995) 1 SCC 551

entities.text: R.D. Hattangadi V/s M/s Pest Control (India) Private Ltd., (1995) 1 SCC 551
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the Hon'ble Supreme Court while dealing with the different heads of compensation in injury cases has held that "this includes a variety of matters such as the inability to walk, run or sit, etc.
We include here too the loss of childhood pleasure such as the ability to freely play, dance, run, etc., the loss of ability to freely move or travel without assistance.
Then, there is the virtual impossibility of marriage as well as a complete loss of the ability to have sex and to have and nurture children."
Applying the same formula to the case on hand this shows that the injuries caused to petitioner has impacted on the enjoyment of his personal life and amenities of life.
Hence, it is necessary to award compensation of Rs.60,000/- under this head.

Admittedly, the respondent No.1 and 2 are the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer is bound to indemnify the respondent No.2.

Hence, respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to petitioner with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a.,

For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.10,33,376/- {future medical expenses shall not carry any interest}, with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release the entire amount in his favour.

In The Civil Appeal No. 8510 Of 2022 Sidram V/S The Divisional Manager, United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
Like wise, in the case of Subulaxmi V/s Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation and another (2012) 10 SCC 177 the Hon'ble Supreme Court awarded compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- towards pain and sufferings to the petitioner.
(b) Loss of enjoyment of life and amenities of life:-
The available on records reveals that the petitioner has sustained fracture injuries at the age of 51 years as on the date of accident.
In R.D. Hattangadi V/s M/s Pest Control (India) Private Ltd., (1995) 1 SCC 551
Applying the same formula to the case on hand this shows that the injuries caused to petitioner has impacted on the enjoyment of his personal life and amenities of life.
Shankar G vs United India Ins Co Ltd on 5 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79862250/

(ii) The occupation of petitioner and quantum of income:- The petitioner has contended that, prior to the accident he was hale and healthy and was Labourer., and he was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
He has not produced any documents to prove the said income.
The petitioner has claimed compensation towards future medical expenditure for follow up treatment.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The income of the petitioner is to be determined.
The annual income of the petitioner shall arrive at Rs.1,92,000/- (Rs.16,000 X 12)
Rs.1,92,000 X 11 X 30/100= Rs.6,33,600/-. Thereby the petitioner is entitled to compensation of Rs.6,33,600/- towards loss of earning capacity and future earnings.
In total, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.80,000/- under this head.
Hence, it is necessary to award compensation of Rs.60,000/- under this head.

Hence, the respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
The respondent No.1 being the insurer is bound to indemnify the respondent No.2.
Hence, respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to petitioner with interest at the rate of 6%
p.a.,
Accordingly, I answer this issue partly in the affirmative.
For the foregoing reasons, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of Rs.10,33,376/- {future medical expenses shall not carry any interest}, with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the realization from respondents.
The respondent No.1 is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 60 days from the date of this order.
Considering the quantum of amount awarded to petitioner, it is ordered to release the entire amount in his favour.
Advocate fee is fixed at 1,500/-.
